title: Doubling the Cube: the Algebraic Reduction of Constructibility
content: The module docstring frames the file as the geometric corollary of the parent's degree computation [ℚ(∛3):ℚ] = 3 (finrank_adjoin_cbrt3): since Mathlib has no development of ruler-and-compass constructibility as a geometric notion, the file adopts the standard algebraic characterization directly as a definition — a real number is constructible iff it lies in a field reached from ℚ by a finite tower of quadratic (degree-2) extensions (IsQuadraticTower). The classical geometry⟺algebra equivalence (each ruler/compass step intersects lines and circles, adjoining at most a square root) is explicitly flagged as the one unformalized, universally-accepted step; everything downstream of the definition is fully verified. It previews the four results: quadratic towers have 2-power degree, hence so do constructible numbers, hence any degree not a power of 2 obstructs constructibility, and ∛3 (degree 3) fails this test — resolving the Delian problem of doubling the cube.
mathContext: Constructible$(\alpha)$ $:\Leftrightarrow$ $\alpha$ lies in a tower $\mathbb{Q}=K_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_n$ with each $[K_{i+1}:K_i]=2$ — taken as the *definition*, with the geometric⟺algebraic equivalence itself classical and unformalized.

title: Quadratic Towers: the Algebraic Shape of Constructibility
content: `IsQuadraticTower : IntermediateField ℚ ℝ → Prop` is defined inductively: the base field ℚ (⊥) is a tower, and any L obtained from a tower K by a single degree-2 step (`relfinrank K L = 2`, i.e. [L:K] = 2) is again a tower. This is the field-theoretic content of Wantzel's reduction: each ruler-and-compass step intersects lines and circles through previously-constructed points and so adjoins at most a square root — a degree-≤2 extension. We take this characterization as the definition; the geometry⟺algebra equivalence itself is the classical, unformalized step.

title: Every Quadratic Tower Has 2-Power Degree
content: `IsQuadraticTower.finrank_eq_two_pow`: any quadratic tower K has Module.finrank ℚ K = 2ⁿ for some n. The proof is induction on the tower. Base: [ℚ:ℚ] = 1 = 2⁰ (IntermediateField.finrank_bot). Step: multiplicativity of degrees in a field tower, IntermediateField.finrank_bot_mul_relfinrank, gives [L:ℚ] = [K:ℚ]·[L:K] = 2ⁿ·2 = 2ⁿ⁺¹. This single induction is where 'each step is quadratic' becomes 'the whole degree is a power of 2'.

title: Constructible Numbers Have 2-Power Degree over ℚ
content: `IsConstructible α` means α lies in some quadratic tower. `finrank_adjoin_eq_two_pow_of_constructible`: then [ℚ⟮α⟯:ℚ] is a power of 2. Proof: ℚ⟮α⟯ is the smallest intermediate field containing α, so ℚ⟮α⟯ ≤ K for the ambient tower K (adjoin_simple_le_iff). The tower law (finrank_bot_mul_relfinrank) makes [ℚ⟮α⟯:ℚ] divide [K:ℚ] = 2ⁿ, and a divisor of a prime power 2ⁿ is itself a power of 2 (Nat.dvd_prime_pow with Nat.prime_two).

title: The General Non-Constructibility Obstruction
content: `not_constructible_of_finrank_ne_two_pow`: any real α whose degree over ℚ is not a power of 2 is non-constructible — the contrapositive of the previous theorem. This is the reusable engine: instantiating it at different degree computations yields doubling-the-cube (degree 3), angle trisection (degree 3 via cos 20°), and non-constructible regular polygons in one stroke.

title: 3 Is Not a Power of 2
content: `three_ne_two_pow`: 3 ≠ 2ⁿ for all n. If 3 = 2ⁿ then 3 ∣ 2ⁿ, and since 3 is prime, Nat.Prime.dvd_of_dvd_pow forces 3 ∣ 2 — false. This is the arithmetic core of the impossibility: the obstruction is purely that 3 and 2 are distinct primes.

title: ∛3 Is Not Constructible — Doubling the Cube Is Impossible
content: `cbrt3_not_constructible`: ∛3 is not ruler-and-compass constructible. The proof applies the general obstruction not_constructible_of_finrank_ne_two_pow and discharges its hypothesis by rewriting with the parent's finrank_adjoin_cbrt3 ([ℚ(∛3):ℚ] = 3) and three_ne_two_pow (3 ≠ 2ⁿ). Geometrically: a cube of double volume would require constructing the length ∛2 (here the prime analogue ∛3) of degree 3 — impossible, since constructible lengths have 2-power degree. This is the formal resolution of the Delian problem.
